title: When Attention Sink Emerges in Language Models
one_line_claim: Attention sinks emerge as a learned phenomenon where models allocate significant attention to early tokens regardless of semantic relevance, driven by softmax normalization.
method_summary: Measures attention sink severity across transformer models using a metric quantifying attention concentration on the first token, then varies training conditions (steps, learning rates, data, architecture) to isolate causes. Sigmoid attention is tested as an alternative to softmax to verify that softmax normalization is the root cause.

key_findings.finding: Attention sinks emerge during training, with magnitude scaling with model size from 60M to 1B+ parameters.
key_findings.quote: We show that the phenomenon is universal: it emerges across model scales from 60M to 1B+ parameters, and becomes more pronounced with larger models.

key_findings.finding: Softmax normalization is the mechanism enabling attention sinks; sigmoid attention eliminates the phenomenon while preserving task performance.
key_findings.quote: We find that the root cause is the softmax normalization: by simply replacing softmax with sigmoid attention, we can eliminate the attention sink without significantly affecting the model's performance.

key_findings.finding: Attention sinks function as implicit key biases that allocate extra attention to the first token without contributing to value computation.
key_findings.quote: Attention sinks act as key biases that store unnecessary attention weight on the first token. Unlike standard key biases, sinks achieve this through the learned attention patterns rather than explicit bias parameters.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both analyze per-token behaviors in transformers to characterize quality phenomena. HERALD monitors logit distributions during inference; this paper identifies attention patterns that compression methods (StreamingLLM) exploit.
differs_on: HERALD predicts compression-induced catastrophic failures (looping, non-termination); this paper explains attention sink emergence, which is mechanistic rather than failure-focused.
HERALD operates during inference with logit-based signals; this paper studies training-time emergence using attention weight analysis.
HERALD targets intervention; this paper provides mechanistic understanding of why models concentrate attention on early tokens.
